scope: P2 email verification implementation, not full account-fields acceptance or real provider delivery.
implemented: Migration 095 adds per-address generations and verification time. An email-update database trigger invalidates old proofs including remove/re-add ABA; existing addresses are unverified by default.

Authenticated owner-bound status/request endpoints use fresh private status and generation CAS. Bots and disabled/banned owners cannot reserve new proofs. Sixty-second durable cooldown and twenty-minute expiry; 32 random bytes with only SHA-256 proof stored.

Public rate-limited confirmation consumes a proof once transactionally and never creates sessions/cookies, restores a disabled account or changes the signed-in identity. Concurrent consumers have one winner and failures roll back.

Configured HTTPS application link uses a fragment, not query parameters. The public client removes the fragment with replacement navigation, requires explicit confirmation instead of GET consumption, and can render while unrelated auth bootstrap is pending.

Resend's existing sender implements a narrow verification capability. Successful acknowledgement requires a nonempty provider message ID. Uncertain failures are not reported as accepted and retain the hashed proof until expiry in case provider delivery succeeded.

TR/EN settings include current address/status, request, cooldown, refresh, capability gating, recoverable errors and stale-account response guards. No provider configuration means explicit unavailable state, never fake delivery.
